title: OSC 633 — VS Code shell integration
summary: OSC 633 marks shell-integration boundaries for VS Code's terminal: prompt start, command start, command executed, and command finished (with exit code and optional duration). It parallels OSC 133 but adds VS Code-specific properties such as the current working directory and an explicit 'E' (command line) marker.

frame.note: OSC 633 ; <command> ST, where <command> is A/B/C/D/E. ST (ESC \) or BEL terminates.

terminator_detail.note: ECMA-48 mandates ST; BEL is widely accepted.

params.name: Prompt start (A)
params.meaning: OSC 633 ; A ST marks the start of a prompt.

params.name: Command start (B)
params.meaning: OSC 633 ; B ST marks the start of the command line (end of prompt).

params.name: Command executed (C)
params.meaning: OSC 633 ; C ST marks the start of command output (end of command line).

params.name: Command finished (D)
params.meaning: OSC 633 ; D [; exitcode] [; duration] ST marks command completion, optionally carrying the exit code and duration in ms.

params.name: Command line (E)
params.meaning: OSC 633 ; E ; <commandline> ST reports the command line text to the terminal.

params.name: Property (P)
params.meaning: OSC 633 ; P ; <key>=<value> ST sets a property such as Cwd (current working directory).

gotchas: VS Code's shell integration also relies on OSC 7 (cwd) and OSC 133 in some setups; 633 is the VS Code-native variant.
D's exit code and duration are optional but recommended for the terminal's command navigation UI.
Command lines reported via E may contain sensitive data; terminals should not persist them without consent.

v1_smoke_test.asserts: OSC 633 subcommands A-E and P render as byte-exact ST-terminated OSC sequences.
